'''Jill Suzanne Barnholtz-Sloan''' is an American [[biostatistician]] and [[data scientist]] specialized in [[cancer epidemiology]] and etiologic investigations of [[Brain tumor|brain tumors]]. She is a senior investigator and associate director for [[informatics]] and data science at the [[National Cancer Institute]]. 

== Life ==
Barnholtz was born to Barbara Barnholtz, a [[Jewish Community Center]] assistant developmental director and Martin Barnholtz, a [[Creve Coeur, Missouri|Creve Coeur]] city councilor.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite news |date=2000-06-18 |title=People in places |pages=2 |work=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/111217863/people-in-places/ |access-date=2022-10-13 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> She completed an M.S. in statistics from the [[University of Texas at Austin]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2021-05-21 |title=Jill S. Barnholtz-Sloan, Ph.D., biographical sketch and research interests - NCI |url=https://dceg.cancer.gov/about/staff-directory/barnholtz-sloan-jill |access-date=2022-10-13 |website=dceg.cancer.gov |language=en}}{{PD-notice}}</ref> Barnholtz earned a Ph.D. in biostatistics from the [[UTHealth School of Public Health]].<ref name=":0" /> Her 2000 dissertation was titled ''Traditional linkage analysis in admixed families''.<ref name=":1">{{Cite thesis |title=Traditional linkage analysis in admixed families |date=2000 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=[[UTHealth School of Public Health]] |oclc=44917142 |last=Barnholtz |first=Jill Suzanne}}</ref> In June 2000, she married [[physician-scientist]] and neurosurgeon [[Andrew E. Sloan]] at the [[Missouri Botanical Garden]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

In 2002, Barnholtz-Sloan was an assistant professor at the [[Karmanos Cancer Institute]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2002-03-19 |title=Ovary cancer is riskier for blacks |pages=57 |work=Detroit Free Press |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/111218382/ovary-cancer-is-riskier-for-blacks/ |access-date=2022-10-13}}</ref> In 2007, she joined the [[Case Comprehensive Cancer Center]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2021-05-14 |title=Director's Message: Jill Barnholtz-Sloan |url=https://case.edu/cancer/about-us/directors-message/directors-message-jill-barnholtz-sloan |access-date=2022-10-13 |website=Case Comprehensive Cancer Center {{!}} School of Medicine {{!}} Case Western Reserve University |language=en}}</ref> She worked in multiple roles in the [[Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine]] (CWRU) and the [[University Hospitals Health System]] (UHHS), which all focused on optimizing the use of data and analytics to advance [[health care]]. She has experience with multi-site, [[brain tumor]], [[patient recruitment]], and [[biological specimen]] collection, storage, and clinical annotation.<ref name=":0" />  She held the Sally S. Morley Designated Professorship/Chair at CWRU.<ref name=":3" />

Barnholtz-Sloan joined the [[National Cancer Institute]] (NCI) in 2021, with a joint appointment as associate director for informatics and data science, in the center for biomedical informatics and information technology and senior investigator in the division of cancer epidemiology and genetics (DCEG).<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jill S. Barnholtz-Sloan, Ph.D. {{!}} CBIIT |url=https://datascience.cancer.gov/about/staff-directory/jill-barnholtz-sloan |access-date=2022-10-13 |website=datascience.cancer.gov}}{{PD-notice}}</ref> Her research portfolio includes descriptive epidemiology studies and etiologic investigations of brain tumors.<ref name=":0" />
